sources.title: Cancelled recurring payment evidence
sources.authority: Prototype policy owner: explicitly fictional, not a bank or legal authority

clauses.text: Provide the original payment reference, merchant, date, charged amount and currency.
Provide when and how cancellation was requested, when it became effective, and any confirmation or reference. Missing confirmation should be recorded as missing; it must not be invented.
A cancellation request does not by itself establish that cancellation was effective before the charge. Conflicting dates or records require human review.
This policy describes evidence collection only. It does not establish dispute eligibility, a chargeback deadline, liability or a refund entitlement.

sources.title: Missing refund evidence
sources.authority: Prototype policy owner: explicitly fictional, not a bank or legal authority

clauses.text: Provide the original purchase reference, merchant, purchase date, amount and currency.
Provide the promised or processed refund date, expected amount and currency, destination payment method and merchant confirmation or refund reference.
A merchant refund record is not proof of a posted account credit. Compare related credits, amounts and destination before describing a refund as received.
No linked record is not proof that a refund was never issued. This corpus specifies no processing deadline; do not declare a refund overdue or guaranteed.

sources.title: Merchant recognition and reported unauthorised activity
sources.authority: Prototype policy owner: explicitly fictional, not a bank or legal authority

clauses.text: Merchant trading names and statement descriptors may differ. Resolve the merchant using bank records before asking whether the customer recognises the payment.
A merchant match, familiar account history or a low anomaly score does not establish customer authorisation.

A report of an unauthorised payment or ongoing card risk requires specialist review. Advise the customer to contact the bank through its official app or the number on the card; this prototype cannot secure a card.
If specialist review is already required, skip the merchant-recognition question. Do not label a payment as proven fraud from customer statements or anomaly signals alone.

sources.title: Multiple charges and wrong-amount evidence
sources.authority: Prototype policy owner: explicitly fictional, not a bank or legal authority

clauses.text: For possible multiple charging, collect both payment references, dates, amounts, currencies, order references and whether the customer made one purchase or separate purchases.
For a wrong-amount concern, distinguish the amount actually charged from the amount agreed or expected. Ask for a receipt and any tip, deposit or later adjustment.
Matching amounts alone do not establish duplicate processing. Different order references are context, not proof that every charge is valid.
Unresolved discrepancies require human review. This corpus does not authorise an automatic refund or decide legal eligibility.
